chapters.title: Matthew Kahona Kasa: The Nativity & The Beatitudes
chapters.summary: The genealogy of Christ and the historic Sermon on the Mount Beatitudes rendered into Tangkhul.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Matthew 5:3-10: Mangazingli ngachamkakhui bingna mathasek-u, kasakei kazingram athumwuisai. Khangaringli ngachirbingna mathasek-u, kasakei athumli khangasak milu sara. Khamanoubingna mathasek-u, kasakei athum mikumo ngaleili ngashansara. Mashung-kasa vang kachamkashi bingna mathasek-u, athumna thingkhalara. Khangacham thotli ngashanbingna mathasek-u, athumli ngashan milu sara.
chapters.english_translation: Blessed are the poor in spirit: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven. Blessed are they that mourn: for they shall be comforted. Blessed are the meek: for they shall inherit the earth. Blessed are they which do hunger and thirst after righteousness: for they shall be filled. Blessed are the merciful: for they shall obtain mercy.
grammar_notes: Suffix -bing marks nominal plurality (ngachirbing = those who mourn).
Optative imperative/blessing suffix -sek-u expresses solemn blessing ('mathasek-u' = blessed be).
exercises: Translate Matthew 5:3 into contemporary spoken Tangkhul.
Identify the grammatical particles functioning as emphatic markers in verse 7.

chapters.title: John Kahona Kasa: The Incarnation & The Light of Men
chapters.summary: Prologue of John in classic Tangkhul syntax, exploring the theological rendering of 'Word' (Tui).
chapters.tangkhul_text: Kaphung-kachungwui thotli Tui li-li-sai, kala Tuichi Varivarali lei, kala Tuichi Varivarasai. Chiya kaphung-kachungli Varivarawui kachungli leisai. Ali vangteina ot kathata pamei sakahaisai; kala sachitheikahai thotwui tharili A matheida khikha masasa mana. Ali ringkapha lei, kala ringkapha china mikumowui mangashan phāsa-e. Kala mangashan chi ngashingli ngashane, kala ngashingna chi mathakakhui-mana.
chapters.english_translation: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. The same was in the beginning with God. All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made. In him was life; and the life was the light of men. And the light shineth in darkness; and the darkness comprehended it not.

vocabulary.meaning: the very beginning, dawn of creation

grammar_notes: Reduplication 'li-li-sai' indicates continuous remote past existence.
Negative verbal frame 'ma-...-mana' in 'mathakakhui-mana' (did not comprehend/overcome).
exercises: Examine the cultural adoption of 'Tui' (word, message, discourse) for Logos in early Tangkhul literature.

chapters.title: The Acts of the Apostles: Pentecost & The First Fellowship
chapters.summary: The descent of the Holy Spirit and early communal living described in Ukhrul dialect.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Acts 2:1-4: Pentecostwui phanit atamli athumpup ngalem akhali ngaburkapam leisai. Chitharan khamathān kazingwui eina hu-hu kaho khongyui kakhangahui akhata rarer, kala athum pamkapam shim tharili chuiserie. Kala athumli meikazat theirei katha tuitak thada kashikaza theiser, kala athum akhakha wui tuingalungli pamserie. Kala athumpup Kazing Mangazing Katharana phāserlaga, kapei tui katek-tek eina tui khangayei honserie.
chapters.english_translation: When the day of Pentecost was fully come, they were all with one accord in one place. And suddenly there came a sound from heaven as of a rushing mighty wind, and it filled all the house where they were sitting. And there appeared unto them cloven tongues like as of fire, and it sat upon each of them. And they were all filled with the Holy Ghost, and began to speak with other tongues.

vocabulary.meaning: to sit gathered in one assembly

grammar_notes: Simile construction 'katha' (like, as of) in 'meikazat theirei katha' (like tongues of flame).
Completive plural verbal aspect '-ser' used repeatedly across clauses.
exercises: Contrast the archaic missionary vocabulary with contemporary church Tangkhul.

chapters.title: Romans 8: Life in the Spirit & Inseparable Love
chapters.summary: St. Paul's exposition of spiritual victory and the hymn of divine love in Tangkhul Naga.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Romans 8:31-39: Vareva ithui ngachaili li-daran, khipana ithuli khangatei sara? Athishur awui Naomayārli mathayala ithupup wui vang mikahaina, A eina shurda khikha mamishukra kachi lei? Khipana ithuli Christawui khangayei eina kashit sara? Ringkaphashi kaji-ra, mathikaji-ra, kazingkaphung-ra? Mano, ot hithatha tharili ithumli ngarukahai A eina ithumna pamei khangaraorap khui-kaphāe.
chapters.english_translation: If God be for us, who can be against us? He that spared not his own Son, but delivered him up for us all, how shall he not with him also freely give us all things? Who shall separate us from the love of Christ? shall tribulation, or distress, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or peril, or sword? Nay, in all these things we are more than conquerors through him that loved us.
grammar_notes: Rhetorical interrogative particle '-ra' forming existential questions.
Postposition 'eina' marking agentive/instrumental cause of triumph.
exercises: List five emotional and theological terms in Romans 8.
Translate verse 38 into Tangkhul preserving the poetic cadences.

chapters.title: 1 Corinthians 13: The Hymn of Christian Love (Khangayeiwui Laa)
chapters.summary: The canonical lyrical translation of 1 Corinthians 13 celebrating enduring love.
chapters.tangkhul_text: 1 Corinthians 13:1-8: I mikumo kala kashang kazingwui tui eina hang-khalangli, iwui tuingalungli khangayei malei-kaji tharan, i khongkhanghui tui katha thada kasaye. Khangayeina khangachon lei, ningkazang lei; khangayeina hingkamachur malei-mana; khangayeina aphasa mathaikhangasang malei-mana, ningkazao malei-mana. Khangayeina kachikathāna khikhali mamatung-mana; tui-ngashungli mathat-e. Chitharan chotkhangashit (faith), ngachikan (hope), khangayei (love) hi kashiko li-leirap sara; chawui ngachaili kaphāmeina khangayeisai.
chapters.english_translation: Though I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, and have not charity, I am become as sounding brass, or a tinkling cymbal. Charity suffereth long, and is kind; charity envieth not; charity vaunteth not itself, is not puffed up. Doth not behave itself unseemly, seeketh not her own, is not easily provoked, thinketh no evil; Rejoiceth not in iniquity, but rejoiceth in the truth. And now abideth faith, hope, charity, these three; but the greatest of these is charity.
grammar_notes: Superlative suffix -mei attached to adjective: kaphāmei (greatest/best).
exercises: Compare the Tangkhul rendering of 'charity/love' (khangayei) with traditional clan kinship terminology.
Memorize the three cardinal virtues in Tangkhul.

chapters.title: Revelation 21-22: The New Jerusalem & The River of Life
chapters.summary: The apocalyptic vision of the New Heaven and New Earth in vivid Tangkhul descriptive language.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Revelation 21:1-4: Kala i kazing kathara kala ngalei kathara theiserie; kasakei kazing khare kala ngalei khare chi ngapaoritserie, kala ngashakazil chi maleilu-mana. Kala i shungkhara shillong kathara, Jerusalem Kathara, Kazingram eina Varivarawui pam eina yorura kapik theiserie. Kala i kaphungli khongyui kakhangahui akhata kapei theiser: 'Kazingramwui shim mikumoli li-leisara!' Kala Varevana athum mikwui mukthi thapup luithatsara; chitharan kathiri maleira, ngachiri maleira, kashamkashi maleilu-mana; kasakei thot khare chi ngapaoritserie.
chapters.english_translation: And I saw a new heaven and a new earth: for the first heaven and the first earth were passed away; and there was no more sea. And I John saw the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband. And God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes; and there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain: for the former things are passed away.

vocabulary.meaning: to pass away completely, vanish, be transformed

grammar_notes: Future negative modal '-lu-mana' denoting absolute cessation of pain.
Cessative verbal compound 'luithat' (to wipe away cleanly).
exercises: Identify the archaic geographic terms utilized by Pettigrew in translating apocalyptic literature.
Discuss how the concept of 'Jerusalem' was introduced into the Naga highland worldview.

chapters.title: Linguistic & Orthographic Lexicon of the 1927 Translation
chapters.summary: Systematic glossary of 50 key loanwords, calques, and dialectal roots documented in the 1927 text.
chapters.tangkhul_text:
Tangkhul Kathara Lairik Tuitam:
1. Varivara -- Almighty Supreme God (traditional Christianized deity term)
2. Kazingram -- Heaven / celestial dominion
3. Mangazing Kathara -- Holy Spirit
4. Naomayār -- Beloved Son
5. Khangayei -- Divine love / agape
6. Mashung-kasa -- Righteousness / moral integrity
7. Kazingkaphung -- Persecution / adversity
8. Chotkhangashit -- Faith / steadfast belief
9. Ngachikan -- Hope / sacred expectation
10. Shillong Kathara -- Holy City / heavenly sanctuary
chapters.english_translation: A comprehensive gloss of theological, moral, and structural Tangkhul terms compiled from the 1927 New Testament, serving as a landmark milestone in the linguistic history of Manipur.
grammar_notes: Historical orthography: usage of 'wui' for genitive instead of modern shortened forms.
Phonetic preservation of final stops and bilabial glides.
exercises: Compare 10 words from this lexicon with their modern counterparts in the TLS 2021 curriculum.
Trace how the word 'Varivara' shifted in semantic domain during the 20th century.

pages.title: Translator's Historical Preface
lines: The completion of the New Testament in Tangkhul Naga represents thirty years
of dedicated translation, commencing in Ukhrul in 1896. With the generous
collaboration of Tangkhul native elders, pastors, and scholars, each book
was painstakingly revised against the original Greek manuscripts.
Published by the British & Foreign Bible Society at the Baptist Mission Press,
Calcutta, 1927. This edition provided the foundation for Tangkhul literacy,

Though I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, and have not
charity, I am become as sounding brass, or a tinkling cymbal. Charity
suffereth long, and is kind; charity envieth not; charity vaunteth not
itself, is not puffed up. Doth not behave itself unseemly, seeketh not
her own, is not easily provoked, thinketh no evil; Rejoiceth not in
iniquity, but rejoiceth in the truth. And now abideth faith, hope,
charity, these three; but the greatest of these is charity.
pages.tangkhul_content: 1 Corinthians 13:1-8: I mikumo kala kashang kazingwui tui eina hang-khalangli, iwui tuingalungli khangayei malei-kaji tharan, i khongkhanghui tui katha thada kasaye. Khangayeina khangachon lei, ningkazang lei; khangayeina hingkamachur malei-mana; khangayeina aphasa mathaikhangasang malei-mana, ningkazao malei-mana. Khangayeina kachikathāna khikhali mamatung-mana; tui-ngashungli mathat-e. Chitharan chotkhangashit (faith), ngachikan (hope), khangayei (love) hi kashiko li-leirap sara; chawui ngachaili kaphāmeina khangayeisai.
pages.english_translation: Though I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, and have not charity, I am become as sounding brass, or a tinkling cymbal. Charity suffereth long, and is kind; charity envieth not; charity vaunteth not itself, is not puffed up. Doth not behave itself unseemly, seeketh not her own, is not easily provoked, thinketh no evil; Rejoiceth not in iniquity, but rejoiceth in the truth. And now abideth faith, hope, charity, these three; but the greatest of these is charity.

pages.tangkhul_content:
Tangkhul Kathara Lairik Tuitam:
1. Varivara -- Almighty Supreme God (traditional Christianized deity term)
2. Kazingram -- Heaven / celestial dominion
3. Mangazing Kathara -- Holy Spirit
4. Naomayār -- Beloved Son
5. Khangayei -- Divine love / agape
6. Mashung-kasa -- Righteousness / moral integrity
7. Kazingkaphung -- Persecution / adversity
8. Chotkhangashit -- Faith / steadfast belief
9. Ngachikan -- Hope / sacred expectation
10. Shillong Kathara -- Holy City / heavenly sanctuary
